prompt.brief: Design a production-line vision inspection system that captures synchronized high-resolution images, detects known and novel defects in real time, and sends safe disposition signals to factory automation.
successSignals: Define camera/line identity, image and part correlation, inspection version, defect taxonomy, confidence, evidence, and disposition semantics.
Meet deterministic line latency while retaining full-resolution evidence; handle lighting drift, missing cameras, duplicate frames, and rare defects.
Separate inference from model training, labeling, review, and factory-control integration; roll out models canary-first without stopping production.
Explain fail-safe versus fail-open decisions, calibration, auditability, privacy, replay, observability, and degraded manual inspection.

functional: Capture and correlate images with part/lot/line identifiers, run versioned inference, classify defects, and persist evidence and decisions.
Send pass/fail/quarantine signals to PLC/MES systems, expose operator review, search, metrics, and feedback for retraining.
Support model rollback, calibration, camera replacement, evidence retention/deletion, replay, and safe operation during network or model failures.
nonFunctional: Meet the agreed false-negative/false-positive targets within the line decision deadline and never block production on training work.
Inspect 1,000 parts per minute across many lines without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100 production lines, 1,000 parts/minute, and 20 cameras per line
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Production-line vision inspection system commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Production-line vision inspection system writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Production-line vision inspection system version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Production-line vision inspection system by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Production-line vision inspection system work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Production-line vision inspection system projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Production-line vision inspection system projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Production-line vision inspection system records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Production-line vision inspection system latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
